hpi_details: 60M presents with progressive yellowing of his skin and eyes over 3 weeks, dark urine, pale stools, and a 15-pound unintentional weight loss.

investigation_events.title: Urgent obstructive jaundice results
investigation_events.availability_message: The urgent liver tests and pancreas-protocol CT are now available; specialist referral should proceed without waiting for tumor-marker testing.

results.value: 3.1 cm hypoenhancing mass in the pancreatic head causing abrupt common bile duct and pancreatic duct cutoff with upstream biliary dilatation; no definite liver metastasis

core_concepts: Painless jaundice + weight loss = pancreatic head mass until proven otherwise.
common_misconceptions: Assuming gallstones without pain in painless jaundice.
dangerous_errors: Delaying CT/MRI in older patients with painless jaundice.
management_principles: CT abdomen (pancreatic protocol), surgical oncology consultation for Whipple evaluation.
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

source_refs.title: SAGES & ACS Evidence-Based Surgical Practice Guidelines

reference_soap.subjective: 60M with painless jaundice, dark urine, pale stool, and weight loss.
reference_soap.objective: Scleral icterus, palpable non-tender gallbladder in RUQ.
reference_soap.assessment: Suspected pancreatic head or periampullary malignancy.
reference_soap.plan: STAT CT Pancreas protocol, LFTs, CA 19-9, GI and Surgery consult.

learning_objectives: Recognize painless jaundice as a hallmark of malignant biliary obstruction.

teaching.one_liner: Painless jaundice, weight loss, and a palpable gallbladder (Courvoisier sign) highly concerning for a pancreatic head tumor.

must_ask.say: When did you first notice the yellowing of your skin and eyes, and has it gotten worse?
Have you had any pain in your belly or back, or has the jaundice been completely painless?
Have you noticed your urine getting darker or your stools becoming pale or clay-colored?
Have you lost weight without trying?
Have you had any itching all over your skin?

history.answer: My eyes and skin have turned yellow, and I've lost a lot of weight without trying.
It started about three weeks ago when my wife noticed my eyes looking yellow, and it has gradually spread across my skin and gotten deeper.
Yes, my urine has turned very dark brown over the past two weeks, almost like cola or strong black tea.
My stools have become very pale and grayish-white, looking almost like putty or clay.
Yes, I have had terrible itching all over my body for the past two weeks, especially at night.
No, I haven't had any belly pain, cramping, or pain after eating at all.
No, I have not had any fever, chills, or night sweats.
No confusion or daytime sleepiness, and I haven't noticed any unusual bruising, bleeding gums, or nosebleeds.
My appetite has dropped off quite a bit over the last month, and I feel worn down and fatigued.
I've lost about fifteen pounds over the past month or so, even though I haven't been dieting.
No, I don't feel lightheaded or short of breath, and I don't look pale other than the yellow tint.
I only have a single beer once or twice a month at social gatherings, and that hasn't changed.
I don't take any prescription drugs, over-the-counter painkillers, herbal remedies, or supplements.
No, I haven't eaten any raw seafood or shellfish, and no one around me has been sick or jaundiced.
I don't have hepatitis, I've never received a blood transfusion, I don't have tattoos or use needles, and I'm only with my wife.
No, I've never had gallstones diagnosed, and I've never had any surgery on my gallbladder or stomach.
No, my stomach hasn't bloated up, and my legs and ankles aren't swollen at all.
I was wondering if something could be wrong with my liver.
With the yellow skin and rapid weight loss, I'm really worried that it might be cancer.
I'm hoping to get some blood tests and an imaging scan today so we can find out what's causing this.
I don't have any chronic medical illnesses like high blood pressure, diabetes, or liver problems.
I've never had any operations or been admitted to a hospital.
I'm not on any medications right now.
I don't have any allergies to medications, foods, or environmental triggers.
I've smoked about a pack of cigarettes a day for thirty years.
I work in an office as an administrative manager and live with my wife.
There is no family history of liver disease, gallbladder problems, or digestive tract cancers.

exam.finding: Blood pressure is 124/78 mmHg, heart rate 74 beats per minute, respiratory rate 16 breaths per minute, body temperature 36.7 C, and oxygen saturation 98% on room air.
Marked bilateral scleral icterus is evident; palpebral conjunctivae show normal pink coloration without pallor.
Generalized jaundice with multiple excoriation marks on the limbs and trunk; no spider angiomas or palmar erythema.
No resting tremor, postural tremor, or asterixis.
Abdomen is flat and symmetrical with no visible distension, prominent collateral veins, caput medusae, or surgical scars.
Normal active bowel sounds heard in all four quadrants; no renal or aortic bruits.
Soft and non-tender throughout; a smooth, tense, non-tender mass consistent with an enlarged gallbladder is palpable in the right upper quadrant.
No inspiratory arrest or focal tenderness on deep palpation beneath the right costal margin.
Smooth, non-tender liver edge palpable 1 cm below the right costal margin; spleen is not palpable.
Percussion note is resonant across the abdomen with no shifting dullness or fluid wave.
No peripheral pitting edema over the ankles or pretibial areas bilaterally.
